fields.meta_description: Build a cookie exchange sign up sheet that closes each cookie once claimed, sets a dozen count for every baker, and flags allergens.
fields.h1: Build a Cookie Exchange Sign-Up Sheet That Plans the Swap
fields.hero_description: Build a cookie exchange sign up sheet that takes each cookie off the list once claimed and tells every baker how many to bake.
fields.features_heading: What the Sheet Settles Before Baking Day
fields.features_subheading: A paper sheet holds names and cookies. This one also blocks repeats, does the dozen math, and keeps allergy details with each batch.
fields.feature_1:
A cookie list that never repeats

List the cookies you want on the table, or let bakers name their own. Once someone claims a cookie, it leaves the list, and the next baker picks from what is still open.
fields.feature_2:
Dozens worked out from the head count

Set a rule such as 6 cookies for each participant. The app multiplies it by the number of sign-ups and tells each baker how many dozen to bring once the list is full.
fields.feature_3:
Allergy details stored with each batch

Each baker ticks what their batch contains, such as peanuts, tree nuts, or wheat. The host gets an email listing every batch with peanuts before the tables are set up.
fields.feature_4:
Recipes collected on the same form

Ask for the recipe along with the cookie name. Every recipe lands in one place, and the host hands out a full set on swap day without chasing anyone by text message.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders that say what to bring

The app emails each baker the week before with their cookie, their dozen count, and the drop-off time. A baker who has not confirmed gets a second email two days out.
fields.feature_6:
Sign-ups kept in a database you own

Every sign-up and its recipe stay in a database you own, ready for next December's swap. On paid plans, export the full code of the sheet to your own GitHub repository.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Cookie Swaps, Run From One Sheet
fields.tab_content_1:
When snickerdoodles are claimed, they leave the list

Fourteen cookie types go up for the Nimbleton Insurance swap. Organizer Sigrun Wenstrom wants no doubles. Five coworkers sign up Monday, and each cookie they claim drops off the list. Wilhelmus Brunvoll opens the sheet next and sees 9 of the 14 still open. Snickerdoodles are gone, and he takes gingerbread men.
fields.tab_content_2:
By the 12th sign-up, each baker owes 6 dozen

Brynja Asplund caps the Cardwyn Lane swap at 12 households, with 6 cookies for each household on the list. That makes 72 cookies per baker, or 6 dozen. When the 12th household signs up, the sheet closes, and every baker gets an email with the 6 dozen count and the Saturday drop-off at her garage.
fields.tab_content_3:
All 3 peanut batches go to a separate table

Peanut butter blossoms are a Troop 418 favorite, but two scouts are allergic. Leader Elske Eskeland asks each family to tick what their batch contains. Of the 18 batches signed up, 3 list peanuts. She gets an email naming all 3 the night before the swap, and they go on their own table in the Fenwyck Elementary gym.
fields.tab_content_4:
One address and a ship-by date reach every member

The 16 members of the Vasquell Street Book Club live in eleven states. Each signs up with a mailing address and the cookie they will ship. When all 16 are in, the app matches each member with another and emails one address and a December 8 ship-by date. Ida Pettigrove sees every match on one page.

fields.howto_title: Making a Cookie Exchange Sign-Up Sheet
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a cookie exchange sign up sheet with no repeat cookies and a clear dozen count for every baker.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the date and a sign-up deadline
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Set one rule for the cookie count
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask what goes into each batch
fields.howto_step_1_des: Set the swap date first, then a sign-up deadline about a week earlier. Bakers need the final head count before they shop for butter and sugar, and the deadline is the moment the sheet closes and the dozen count goes out.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Choose how many cookies every baker owes each participant, such as 6, and put it at the top of the sheet. With 12 sign-ups, that rule asks 6 dozen of every baker. Cap sign-ups if the total gets bigger than one home oven can handle.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Name the cookies you want, or let bakers write in their own and check each one against the others. Two trays of sugar cookies make a dull swap. Keep a write-in slot open for family recipes that are not on your list.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add a checkbox for each allergen you care about, including peanuts, tree nuts, milk, eggs, wheat, and sesame. Bakers tick them when they sign up. Use the answers to give batches with peanuts a table of their own on swap day.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Collect the recipe with the sign-up
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put a recipe field right under the cookie name, with room for ingredients and bake time. Bakers fill it in once. Copies of every recipe can go home with the cookies, and nobody has to remember to bring a printed card.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Plan the drop-off and the packaging
fields.howto_step_6_des: Tell bakers where to bring their cookies and how to pack them, such as tins or boxes that each hold a dozen. Show the drop-off time and place on the confirmation screen each baker sees right after signing up.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Describe it to Emergent, then test
fields.howto_step_7_des: Write a sentence or two about the swap: the cookie rule and the cap, plus who gets which email and when. Emergent builds the sheet from that description. Sign up twice with test names and check that a claimed cookie leaves the list.

faq_plan.q: What is a cookie exchange sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: A cookie exchange sign up sheet is the list where each guest at a cookie swap writes their name and the cookie they will bake. An online one can also hold each batch's allergy details and recipe, and tell every baker how many cookies to bring.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a cookie exchange sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Describe the swap in plain English on Emergent's AI form builder: the cap on sign-ups, the per-person cookie rule, and the questions to ask. Emergent builds the form and a database for every answer. Change any part later by asking for it in plain English.

faq_plan.q: What should a cookie exchange sign up sheet ask each baker?
faq_plan.a: Ask for a name, an email for reminders, the cookie they will bring, and what the batch contains. A recipe field is worth adding too. Keep the whole form on one screen, because people tend to sign up from a phone between other things.

faq_plan.q: Can a cookie exchange sign up sheet also take cookie orders?
faq_plan.a: It can, but keep the two apart. A swap trades homemade cookies for free, while a sale needs prices, quantities, and pickup times. Build a separate cookie order form for selling, and keep the exchange sheet for the people trading batches.

faq_plan.q: Can a cookie exchange sign up sheet stop two people from baking the same cookie?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the cookies come from a list. Each claimed cookie closes for everyone who signs up after. Write-in names are harder to match, since chocolate chip and choc chip look different to software. Send write-ins to the host, who approves each one or asks the baker to pick again.

faq_plan.q: How can a cookie exchange sign up sheet tell each baker how many cookies to make?
faq_plan.a: It multiplies your per-person rule by the number of sign-ups once the sheet closes. With 6 cookies per participant and 10 bakers, each one makes 60 cookies, or 5 dozen. Emergent builds that math into the sheet from a plain-English description, and the sheet has no cap on responses.

faq_plan.q: How do I collect allergy information on a cookie exchange sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Put allergen checkboxes beside the cookie name, plus a notes field for anything else. Include sesame: the FDA lists it as the 9th major food allergen recognized by the United States. The answers stay attached to each batch, and the host can sort by them before setting the tables.

faq_plan.q: Can bakers share their recipes through the cookie exchange sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add a recipe field with ingredients and bake time, and each recipe saves with the baker's sign-up. After the swap, the host can email the full set to every baker. On Emergent, the recipes live in a database you own, and next year's sheet can start from them.

faq_plan.q: Does a cookie exchange sign up sheet work for a swap by mail?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask each baker for a mailing address and give the swap a ship-by date. Once sign-ups close, the app can pair each baker with another and email them one address. Set the ship-by date early in December, and ask for sturdy tins that survive the trip.

faq_plan.q: Can a cookie exchange sign up sheet send reminder emails before swap day?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The email a week out lands while bakers still have time to shop for butter and flour, and the one two days out goes only to people who have not confirmed. For an office swap, the app can post the same reminder to a Slack channel.

plan.angle: Searchers for cookie exchange sign up sheet find printable grids with a name column and a cookie column, and the host still has to spot duplicate recipes, work out how many dozen each baker owes, and chase allergy notes by text. This page shows the sheet doing that work in four real swaps: an office swap where a claimed cookie leaves the list, a street swap where the baking count follows the head count, a scout troop swap that flags peanut batches for their own table, and a book club swap by mail that gives each member one address to ship to.
